title: Every Afternoon She Walked
text:
Every afternoon she walked

with her mother along the Landstrasse


And on the corner

of the Schmiedtor

every afternoon


Hitler was there

waiting for her to see her pass


The taxis and buses

were full of kisses


And sweethearts rented boats

on the Danube.


But he did not know how

to dance. He never dared

to speak to you


Afterward she passed without her mother

with a cadet.


And afterward

she did not pass again.


From there later

the Gestapo

the annexation of Austria,


The world war.
editorial_note: The source says 'Australia,' but the historical sequence points to Austria; the translation follows that context.

title: I Remember So Many
text:
I remember so many

beautiful girls

who have existed


All the beauties

of Troy and those of Achaea


And those of Thebes and

of Propertius's Rome


And many of them

let love pass by,


And died, and for

centuries have not existed


You who are beautiful

now in the streets of

Managua


One day you will be like them

from a distant time,


When the gas stations

are romantic ruins.


Remember the

beauties of the

streets of Troy!


Ah, your pitilessness


More cruel

than Tachito.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the sweep from ancient beauties to Managua and the final political sting against Tachito.

title: Triumphal March
text:
Here comes the general

now... the general

here comes the general

mounted on his white horse, surrounded

by guards and bodyguards and deputies and pockmarked whores

he passes beneath the triumphal arch

of paper

LONG LIVE THE LIBERAL PARTY!

on his fat sweaty chest shine

the shit-colored medals. Rockets

explode. The band plays.

LONG LIVE GENERAL SOMOZA! He smiles

with fear, looking everywhere. The horse's

hooves slip in the vomit of the drunks

LONG LIVE THE NATIONALIST LIBERAL PARTY
editorial_note: The translation preserves the grotesque triumphal procession and Cardenal's deliberately coarse anti-Somoza diction.

title: In Costa Rica
text:
In Costa Rica

the oxcart drivers sing


They walk with

mandolins on the roads


And the carts

are painted like macaws,


And the oxen go

with colored ribbons


And little bells

and flowers on their horns.


When it is the coffee

harvest in Costa Rica,


And the carts go

loaded with coffee.


And there are bands

in the town squares,


And in San José

the balconies and windows

are full of girls and flowers


And the girls

circle around in the park.


And the president

walks on foot

in San José.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the civic contrast of a singing, walkable Costa Rica with a president on foot.

title: I Give You, Claudia, These Verses
text:
I give you, Claudia, these verses,

because you are their owner.


I have written them simply

so that you will understand them.


They are for you alone,

but if they do not interest you,

one day they will be spread,

perhaps through all of Spanish America...


And if the love that dictated them,

you too despise,


others will dream

of this love

that was not for them.


And perhaps you will see,

Claudia,

that these poems,

(written to conquer you)

awaken

in other couples

in love who read them

the kisses that in you

the poet did not awaken.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the playful threat that poems meant for Claudia may move everyone except Claudia.
